name: The Mr. T Experience
label: Lookout!
lede: Berkeley's wittiest pop-punk band ran through a dozen lineups, kept a Lookout! catalog going for twenty years, and its singer became a novelist.

eras.title: Product, just another in the line
eras.text: Four Bay Area kids name a band after a 1985 pop-culture fad and start writing Ramones-and-Buzzcocks songs about girls. Their first records come out on other people's labels, one of which folds under them.

q: Just another in the long line of products.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience · Wikipedia: Frank Portman
years.h: [[Dr. Frank|9c7174de-8941-422f-a17b-9ae9d14dc534]] and friends start The Mr. T Experience in Berkeley
years.p: Frank Portman, Byron Stamatatos, Jon von Zelowitz and Alex Laipenieks form the band in summer 1985, taking the name from Mr. T's product saturation that year.
years.xp:
Portman and Stamatatos had played together in a high school band, the Bent Nails, in Millbrae. Portman has said the joke was that they would be "just another in the long line of products."

The band grew up alongside the punk scene around 924 Gilman Street and the Lookout! label.

years.h: Everybody's Entitled to Their Own Opinion arrives on Disorder
years.p: The debut album comes out in July 1986. Encyclopedia.com describes it as self-released; Wikipedia credits Disorder Records.

years.h: Night Shift at the Thrill Factory lands on Rough Trade
years.p: The band's second album is released on the UK indie label's American arm.

years.h: Big Black Bugs Bleed Blue Blood, then Rough Trade closes
years.p: The EP appears in 1989 and Rough Trade shuts down shortly after, leaving the band without a label.
years.xp: Bassist Byron Stamatatos also left in 1989 and Aaron Rubin took over on bass, the lineup that would sign to Lookout!.

years.h: Byron Stamatatos out, Aaron Rubin in on bass
years.p: Stamatatos, Portman's friend from the Bent Nails, leaves; Rubin takes the bass chair.

eras.title: Lookout! moves in
eras.text: The band signs to the fledgling Berkeley label that will be its home for the next two decades, and makes its first records that fans still play.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Mr. T Experience
years.h: Making Things with Light: the first CD on Lookout!
years.p: Portman's vocals move to the front on the band's first Lookout! album, reported as the label's first CD release.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com calls it the turning point, the record where Dr. Frank was "finally able to fully realize his melodic designs."

years.h: Signed to Lookout!, Berkeley's young punk label
years.p: After the Rough Trade collapse, the band lands at Lookout! Records and stays through its whole run.

years.h: Milk Milk Lemonade comes out on Lookout!
years.p: The album follows the band's first European tour, which included recording the live EP Strum ünd Bang, Live!? in Spain.

years.h: Jon von Zelowitz quits after the first European tour
years.p: His exit nearly ends the band. A brief reunion attempt does not hold, and the band carries on as a trio.

eras.title: Musical chairs
eras.text: Drummers and bassists come and go, and Portman weighs graduate school. The band survives, gets a new rhythm section and finds its sound.

years.h: Gun Crazy EP, the trio's first release
years.p: With Portman, Rubin and Laipenieks, the three-piece puts out the EP and then the album Our Bodies Our Selves.
years.xp: Laipenieks then declined to tour and left, which brought another near-breakup. Portman considered graduate school and Rubin joined Samiam. Jim "Jym" Pittman took over on drums.

years.h: Alex Laipenieks leaves; Jym Pittman takes the drums
years.p: The original drummer quits rather than tour. Pittman, who will stay for two decades, comes in.

years.h: ...And the Women Who Love Them restarts the band
years.p: Rubin returns for the EP, which Wikipedia says gave the group new creative energy.

years.h: Our Bodies, Our Selves
years.p: Encyclopedia.com cites it as proof of the band's growing songwriting sophistication.

years.h: Aaron Rubin leaves again for Samiam; Joel Reader joins
years.p: Reader, who first heard the band at age 11, takes over on bass and completes the trio that would last four years.

eras.title: A record a year
eras.text: The most stable lineup since the late 1980s, Portman, Reader and Pittman, turns out an album every year and lands songs in movies.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Is Dead · Trouser Press
years.h: Love Is Dead, produced by Kevin Army
years.p: Recorded in 1995 at Bay Records and Emeryville Recording Company, it is the first album by the Portman, Reader and Pittman trio.
years.xp: Trouser Press called it "a wonderful album" and Metroactive named it a can't-miss record of the year. One track sets a poem by Dorothy Parker.

years.h: "I Just Wanna Do It With You" goes to Hollywood in Glory Daze
years.p: The band contributes songs to the 1996 college comedy starring Ben Affleck, including "Even Hitler Had a Girlfriend."

years.h: Revenge Is Sweet, and So Are You
years.p: Portman is the last original member and jokes the band is now the "MTX Starship."
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com says Portman used the joke name for the rotating lineup.

years.h: Dr. Frank's side project, The Bomb Bassets, releases Take a Trip
years.p: Portman and Dallas Denery record as the Bomb Bassets.

years.h: Road to Ruin, a Ramones cover album
years.p: The band pays tribute to its biggest influence with a full-record Ramones cover set, and a song lands in a Disney TV film, My Date with the President's Daughter.

years.h: Alcatraz, and Portman's solo debut
years.p: The band's fourth record in four years arrives alongside Show Business Is My Life, Portman's solo album.

years.h: Joel Reader leaves; Gabe Meline joins on bass
years.p: Organist Erik Noyes also plays with the band from 1999 to 2000.

eras.title: Smaller stages, a new four-piece
eras.text: Touring thins out, but Portman keeps writing songs and the band reforms as a four-piece.

years.h: The Miracle of Shame EP
years.p: The band's last EP of the Meline era.

years.h: Gabe Meline leaves
years.p: The bassist departs after sporadic touring.

years.h: Ted Angel and Bobby J Jordan join, making a four-piece
years.p: It is the first four-piece lineup in ten years. Portman's solo collection Eight Little Songs also appears this year.

years.h: Yesterday Rules
years.p: The band's final Lookout! album is followed by only limited touring.

eras.title: Dr. Frank, novelist
eras.text: Portman turns into a best-selling young-adult author but never quite shelves the band.

years.h: King Dork is published
years.p: Portman's first novel about a teenage record nerd is optioned for film by Gary Sanchez Productions and later Sony Pictures. The band goes quiet after 2005.

years.h: Andromeda Klein follows
years.p: Portman's second novel appears in 2009.

years.h: Jaz Brown takes over on drums
years.p: Jym Pittman's long tenure ends; Brown joins Portman, Angel and Jordan.

years.h: King Dork Approximately is published
years.p: The sequel novel appears in 2014.

years.h: King Dork Approximately: The Album
years.p: The band's eleventh studio album is released with the reissued novel and a download code, followed by Shards volumes in 2016, 2017 and 2021.
years.xp: Shards Vol. 1 (2016), Vol. 2 (2017) and Vol. 3 (2021) collect further new songs.

years.h: Original drummer Alex Laipenieks dies
years.p: Wikipedia lists his death in 2021; no cause is given in sources I found.
